item.title: Jaylen Brown addresses Jayson Tatum beef rumors, takes subtle shot at former Celtics teammate
item.description: Jaylen Brown addresses Jayson Tatum beef rumors, takes subtle shot at former Celtics teammate originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Jaylen Brown acknowledged that there is no “beef” between him and former Boston Celtics teammate Jayson Tatum. But … “It might be a little lamb chops and some gravy,” Brown said after the 76ers ’ 127-116 win over the Milwaukee Bucks Saturday night at Xfinity Mobile Arena. “You know what I mean? He should stay ready at all times.” Petre Thomas-Imagn Images Things will be interesting when the Sixers (3-0) host the Boston Celtics on Nov. 10 in the first of four series meetings between Atlantic Division rivals. The Celtics (1-1) shipped the five-time All-Star and 2024 NBA Finals MVP to the Sixers in a blockbuster trade for Paul George and multiple draft picks. On Instagram, Brown posted a blue hat, which is the symbol for “cap,” meaning something is untruthful, in response to Tatum saying in a video that he was “just as much caught off guard as the rest of the world” by the trade. Tatum responded to Brown’s symbol after Boston beat the New York Knicks on Friday. “I don’t have any animosity or beef, or ill will towards him,” the Celtic six-time All-Star said. “I think the toughest part is since he’s not on the Celtics anymore, the narrative or the conversations haven’t been enough about what we accomplished — all the games we won, winning a championship, how we’ve grown together. It’s turned into this drama type of thing.” Tatum added that he'd like to talk with Brown to clear things up and reach an understanding. “He just turned 30,” Tatum said. “I’m 28 with two kids. It should be more about winning a championship. This ain’t no Shaq and Kobe. There is no beef. That’s not my thing.” Brown, who scored 27 points on his 30th birthday on Saturday, doesn’t plan to talk to Tatum before the teams’ meeting on Nov. 10. "We both got so much stuff in front of us," he said. "So, at the end of the day, … he’s got to do what he’s got to do for his team. I got to do what I do for my team. Jayson's a great guy. Like I said, great family, hell of a basketball player, hell of a PR team. “There's no beef, but it might be a little lamb chop." Tatum and Brown thrived as a pairing during their nine years together in Boston. The Celtics, however, decided Tatum was the player they wanted to build around and traded Brown in what was essentially a cost-cutting move.

item.title: PSG enter race for highly-rated Real Madrid youth target with Barcelona also keen – report
item.description: PSG enter race for highly-rated Real Madrid youth target with Barcelona also keen – report Manchester United youngster JJ Gabriel has been in the headlines in recent weeks as he looks to secure a move away from the English club. Gabriel has been pushing for an exit for a while now , with Barcelona and Real Madrid emerging as the frontrunners for his signature. Now, according to Diario SPORT , Los Blancos face growing competition in their pursuit of the 16-year-old, with PSG joining the race. The French club have opened discussions with the 16-year-old’s representatives, while Real Madrid are also intensifying their contacts with the player’s entourage. PSG emerge as serious competition for Real Madrid Gabriel recently turned 16 and is regarded as one of the most promising young talents in English football. The French champions are hoping to convince Gabriel with an attractive sporting project and a financial package that could prove difficult for their competitors to match. Madrid, meanwhile, are working to strengthen their position in the race, although no agreement has been reached thus far. JJ Gabriel is out shopping for a new club. (Photo by Naomi Baker/Getty Images) Barcelona also remain firmly interested and could hold an advantage in one important area. The youngster is said to be interested in the Catalan club’s playing philosophy. They also have a reputation for trusting and developing young players, another factor that could influence the teenager. While that may be his preference, it does not guarantee a move to the Camp Nou over the Santiago Bernabeu or the Parc des Princes. Madrid must present a convincing development plan The financial aspect could become particularly important as competition for Gabriel increases. Barcelona are unwilling to enter an expensive bidding war for a player who has yet to make his official Manchester United first-team debut. Gabriel also holds an EU passport through his Irish ancestry, potentially helping to facilitate a move to Spain at 16. Real Madrid need to find a way to convince JJ Gabriel to join them. (Photo by Naomi Baker/Getty Images) Manchester United, meanwhile, retain the player’s rights and are still hoping to secure his future. For Madrid, the challenge goes beyond competing financially with PSG. Gabriel is seeking a clear pathway towards senior football. Luis Enrique also has a good track record of giving youngsters minutes, especially in Ligue 1, where PSG tend to rotate quite often. Real Madrid have the resources and reputation to attract elite young prospects, but they also need to offer a clear pathway. With Barcelona offering an established youth-development model and PSG prepared to compete financially, Madrid cannot depend on prestige alone. It remains to be seen what the future holds for JJ Gabriel and where he plays his football in the upcoming seasons.

"You know, we treat everybody equal; just because you wear orange and black or red and black, you're still all the same. You still bleed red," Bobby Grizzard, a former Massillon police officer, said. "When I grew up in the '70s, you would never tailgate with somebody from Canton. But now with the internet, we're in touch with far more people than we used to be, and I think at least here they're very civil and we don't have to worry about shenanigans." Peoples Baptist Church pastor Walter Arrington, a Massillon alum, agreed. He recalled how in past years the game can be "electrically charged" and at times split the cities. "It's a good scene when people are disciplined. You can enjoy people even if your team doesn't win and that's where we got to get to," he said. "There's more important stuff than this (game). Bobby Grizzard emphasized the passion his wife has for cooking. Noting how she takes time to cook barbecue, chicken, and pulled pork dinners for dozens of homeless people on the holidays. With the event first starting when Brandyn Grizzard and his siblings played for Massillon in the early 2000s, he's in awe of how much it has grown. So to be able to see people you haven't seen in quite a few years, it's a blessing." This article originally appeared on The Repository: Tailgate brings Massillon, McKinley fans together

item.title: ‘Waste of Height,’ ‘Needs to Drink More Creatine or Something’ — NBA Fans Baffled as Victor Wembanyama Gets Swatted in Back-to-Back Games
item.description: ‘Waste of Height,’ ‘Needs to Drink More Creatine or Something’ — NBA Fans Baffled as Victor Wembanyama Gets Swatted in Back-to-Back Games The San Antonio Spurs finally got off the mark on Saturday night. After dropping their previous games against the Oklahoma City Thunder and the Houston Rockets, the Spurs earned their first win of the 2026-27 season with a 122-106 victory over the Dallas Mavericks. Despite the result, one moment involving Victor Wembanyama drew plenty of reaction on social media. NBA Fans Trolled Victor Wembanyama After He Got Blocked on Saturday Night During the first half of Saturday’s game , Zaccharie Risacher, who made his first regular-season start for Dallas with Cooper Flagg and Kyrie Irving sidelined, showed his defensive capabilities. As Wembanyama attempted to score near the basket, Risacher timed his leap perfectly and blocked the 7’4″ center’s shot. Fan reactions soon followed. Interestingly, something similar happened during the Spurs’ previous game. With Houston leading by two, San Antonio called a timeout with five seconds remaining. On the ensuing possession, Wembanyama got the ball in the paint for a potential game-tying layup, but Amen Thompson rejected the attempt with less than a second left. Thompson timed his leap perfectly and swatted the attempt cleanly at the rim. MORE: ‘Freak Athlete,’ ‘Unreal’ – Kevin Durant, NBA Fans Lose It Over Amen Thompson’s ‘Insane’ Game-Winning Block vs. Victor Wembanyama Fred VanVleet then secured the rebound and sank two free throws to seal the victory. After getting blocked again on Saturday, one fan argued that Wembanyama isn’t taking advantage of his height. “Waste of height smh should’ve went to me,” the fan wrote , whereas another one said , “Wemby aura evaporated bro not seen him get rejected this much bro. Blocked by Zaccharie Risacher is not real.” Risacher finished with 11 points, 4 rebounds, 2 assists, 1 steal, and 2 blocks in 32 minutes, while Wembanyama put up 23 points, 7 rebounds, and 4 blocks. Still, some fans suggested that he isn’t playing at the level he used to, even while helping his team to its first win of the season. “This man is washed beyond repair,” said one user, whereas another one said , “Wemby has to leave my league immediately this guy is garbage.” One X user took a different approach to the situation. They jokingly suggested that Wembanyama needed a physical boost to avoid getting rejected at the rim. “Wemby needs to drink more creatine or something. This is becoming absurd,” the user wrote . For Wembanyama, the most important takeaway from Saturday’s matchup was San Antonio finally getting into the win column. However, with fans closely watching his every move, the Spurs star will likely continue to face scrutiny whenever things don’t go his way. This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

item.title: Penn State Opens as Favorite Over Purdue
item.description: WEST LAFAYETTE, INDIANA - NOVEMBER 16: Devin Mockobee #45 of the Purdue Boilermakers runs the ball against the Penn State Nittany Lions at Ross-Ade Stadium on November 16, 2024 in West Lafayette, Indiana. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images Penn State is still seeking its first conference victory of the season as we reach the final Saturday of October. They may not have to wait much longer according to the oddsmakers, as the Nittany Lions are listed as a 7.5-point favorite over Purdue per FanDuel. Penn State enters the game on a four-game skid dating back to the start of Big Ten play. Losses have piled up against Wisconsin, Northwestern, USC and Michigan behind an offense that regularly stalls out and a defense that has difficulty getting off the field. The Nittany Lions are coming off a bye week as they look to turn their season around. Purdue also enters the season at 3-4, although there is more optimism around the Boilermakers. Despite being a common pick to finish dead last in the Big Ten, Purdue has showed promise by knocking off Illinois and Minnesota for a 2-2 record in conference play. The Boilermakers are also coming off a bye, with their last game a 38-26 loss to Washington on Friday, Oct. 16. Penn State and Purdue will kick off on Saturday from Beaver Stadium at 4:15 p.m., with the game airing on BTN.

item.title: SC Freiburg’s Philipp Treu has always admired Bayern Munich star Joshua Kimmich
item.description: (Photo by Federico Gambarini/picture alliance via Getty Images) Philipp Treu was one of the brightest talents showcased under Jürgen Klopp during the September international break. The SC Freiburg right-back jumped immediately into the squad and did everything asked of him—and perhaps more—catching the eyes of virtually all fans. While Treu isn’t exactly a young prospect, the 25-year-old defender could have a large future ahead of him and seems like the answer at right-back after Klopp deservedly moved Joshua Kimmich back into midfield. Interestingly enough, when asked who impressed Treu the most during the international break, Treu was quick to name none other than Joshua Kimmich. “As a kid and teenager, I always looked up to him. It was impressive to get to know him as a person, but also to watch him on the pitch. It starts right from the warm-up. He’s already sweating while riding the bike and always gives 100%. You always hear about how extremely ambitious he is and how badly he wants to win—but experiencing that for myself was really cool. I can also take that mentality into my own life. He wants to win every game and always get the very best out of himself. That makes him a role model for many,” Treu told Bild , as captured by @iMiaSanMia . While many fans were displeased by what Kimmich delivered on the pitch during the international break, his impact was certainly felt around the Germany camp and is making a big impression on the newcomers. While Kimmich might be a guaranteed starter with the national team, he will without a doubt remain a leader on and off the pitch moving forward. Join the conversation! item.title: UFC 333, The Morning After: Old Man Volk, King Of The Featherweight Pantheon
item.description: ABU DHABI, UNITED ARAB EMIRATES - OCTOBER 24: Alexander Volkanovski of Australia punches Movsar Evloev of Russia in the UFC featherweight championship fight during the UFC 333 event at Etihad Arena on October 24, 2026 in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates. (Photo by Jeff Bottari/Zuffa LLC) Featherweight is the division of great UFC champions. Jose Aldo . Conor McGregor . Max Holloway . Alexander Volkanovski . Ilia Topuria . That’s it. The belt infrequently changes hands, and when it does, the new champion goes on to establish himself as one of the very best in the world at a minimum. Seriously, Conor McGregor is the weakest name on that list in terms of career accomplishment, and he was one of the most special fighters to ever live while on the 145-pound roster. After UFC 333 , however, there’s no argument that Volkanovski stands alone … which hurts to admit as a Jose Aldo truther. Two years ago, Volkanovski’s championship career was over. The simple facts were looming large for “The Great.” Not only had he lost three of his last four fights, but the two men to defeat him three times were the pair of champions in the two possible divisions in which Volkanovski competes. There was no path back to gold, and Volkanovski lost consecutive fights via knockout. Retirement would’ve been a completely reasonable play. Instead, fortune favored Volkanovski, and luck plays a role in the career of every fighter. Volkanovski could not control Topuria or Islam Makhachev , but both men opted to move up a division. Suddenly, the road back to Featherweight gold was … well, not exactly clear, but at least possible. And so Volkanovski denied every statistic in the book about age and champions to outclass Diego Lopes — bigger, more powerful, and seven years younger — not once but twice. Lopes simply didn’t have the depth of skill to keep up with the crafty veteran. Last night, Volkanovski proved he’s not just a bad style matchup for Lopes but No. 1-ranked Movsar Evloev as well. The Australian didn’t struggle particularly hard to deny, escape, and/or reverse Evloev’s takedowns, and this is an undefeated fighter who has wrestled every opponent he’s ever faced. Instead, fortune favored Volkanovski, and luck plays a role in the career of every fighter. Volkanovski could not control Topuria or Islam Makhachev , but both men opted to move up a division. Suddenly, the road back to Featherweight gold was … well, not exactly clear, but at least possible. And so Volkanovski denied every statistic in the book about age and champions to outclass Diego Lopes — bigger, more powerful, and seven years younger — not once but twice. Lopes simply didn’t have the depth of skill to keep up with the crafty veteran. Last night, Volkanovski proved he’s not just a bad style matchup for Lopes but No. 1-ranked Movsar Evloev as well. A lot of us remembered Volkanovski’s tremendous first anti-wrestling performance (in defeat) against Makhachev and expected Evloev to have a hell of a time, and those predictions were justified. The Australian didn’t struggle particularly hard to deny, escape, and/or reverse Evloev’s takedowns, and this is an undefeated fighter who has wrestled every opponent he’s ever faced. Does Evloev being a favorable stylistic matchup for Volkanovski diminish Volkanovski’s accomplishment? Absolutely not! Evloev is an awful matchup for many great fighters, including some of those aforementioned past champions. Furthermore, Volkanovski tends to be a really bad style matchup for most opponents because he’s just that damn good, so deeply skilled that he wins dominantly in all sorts of fashions and make great opponents look limited. Volkanovski’s second championship reign has left him undeniable. There is no longer a question of whether Volkanovski is the greatest 145-pound fighter of all time. Instead, he should now be featured prominently in conversations with the likes of Jon Jones and Georges St. Pierre in the all-time lists. item.description: Motorsport photo The 2027 Dakar Rally will no longer take place in Saudi Arabia as originally planned, with organisers Amaury Sport Organisation (ASO) and Saudi Motorsport Company (SMC) confirming that the event will be relocated to a different region. However, the 49th edition of Dakar will still go ahead as planned from 1-15 January, with a new venue set to be announced in the coming days. item.title: Vanoli: Fiorentina ‘improving’ despite 2-1 loss vs. Inter
item.description: Vanoli: Fiorentina ‘improving’ despite 2-1 loss vs. Inter Fiorentina coach Paolo Vanoli feels his team is ‘improving’ despite a 2-1 away defeat at Inter : ‘We must keep our heads held high.’ The Tuscans took the lead in the second half with a stunning goal from Alex Jimenez, but late strikes from Marcus Thuram and Piotr Zielinski gave Inter all three points at San Siro in Sunday’s Serie A lunchtime game. FLORENCE, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 20: Head coach Paolo Vanoli manager of ACF Fiorentina reacts during the Serie A match between ACF Fiorentina and SSC Napoli at Stadio Artemio Franchi on September 20, 2026 in Florence, Italy. (Photo by Gabriele Maltinti/Getty Images) “We knew Inter were strong, but I think we played a great game,” Vanoli told DAZN. “We have improved in many aspects. Obviously, we had a couple of chances to score the second. This isn’t the first time Inter have made a comeback. We need to realise that we are improving. I’m sorry for the lads because they deserved an important win. We must keep our heads held high and keep this up. “We must not look to last season. We are looking for the right suit. We are trying to win at all costs; the table doesn’t look pretty, and it makes things hectic, but I think this team is becoming a team and must keep going like this,” continued the Fiorentina coach. “Going forward, I think these can be important games. Then the result determines morale, and we must look for it. Since I arrived, we have deserved more in some games, including against Genoa. We met a strong team today; we held on, and we understood that we can do well.” MILAN, ITALY – OCTOBER 25: Piotr Zielinski of FC Internazionale Milano celebrates scoring his team’s second goal with teammates during the Serie A match between FC Internazionale and ACF Fiorentina at Stadio Giuseppe Meazza on October 25, 2026 in Milan, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) Vanoli also explained why he replaced Jimenez and Mastantuono in the second half, introducing Dodo and Wilfried Gnonto, even if Inter had been struggling on that side of the pitch: “That is why I brought on two fresh players. I brought on Dodo and Willy because I thought Inter would struggle and force Mkhitaryan to track back,” the Viola coach said.

item.title: Detroit Red Wings takeaway: Loss to Flames shows how much growth is still needed
item.description: Just as the Detroit Red Wings were making progress, they regressed. A rule of thumb regarding road trips is that a successful one points-wise matches the number of stops. The Wings could have put themselves in a great position heading into the finale of their longest trip this month but flunked. The 4-1 loss at the Calgary Flames on Saturday, Oct. 24, snapped a six-game point streak. “They were obviously better than us in multiple areas. Look at the special teams alone,” Red Wings coach Todd McLellan told reporters. “I thought it was one of our poorer nights as far as execution goes. When we did work hard and got offensive opportunities, passes were in the skates, they were too far ahead, so just a lack of overall details cost us. OFF-ICE: Dylan Larkin has given Detroit Red Wings 10 teams as trade options The Wings (4-4-3) were 0 for 2 on power plays and 0 for 2 on penalty kills. Their only goal came from Andrew Copp early in the second period − after which the Flames scored three straight times on John Gibson. The trip wraps up Monday at the Edmonton Oilers , who are 8-2-1. McLellan's criticism that it was one of the Wings' poorer efforts is pretty damming. Beset as they are by the turmoil of Dylan Larkin wanting to play for another team and Simon Edvinsson absent because of a contract stalemate, the Wings had shown resilience on this trip with rallying from a three-goal deficit to squeeze a point out of a 4-3 shootout loss at the Seattle Kraken and then winning 5-2 in Vancouver the next stop. The Flames game shows how far the Wings still have to grow. The Calgary team is 4-6-0, near the bottom of the Western Conference, but have won three games in a row. That's the traction the Wings seek as they try to gain a foothold in the Eastern Conference. Contact Helene St. James at Hstjames@freepress.com. The coach who once declared “today, tomorrow and always, Barcelona in my heart,” and claimed he would only ever go to Real Madrid to destroy them, has been entrusted with attempting to bring about the destruction of Barcelona. item.title: Change captain? Play the kids? How to solve the problems at Manchester United
item.description: The beleaguered Michael Carrick’s job is on the line, but there are steps he can take to revive the stricken club The big question as Bournemouth arrive for Sunday’s 2pm kick-off at Old Trafford is whether Michael Carrick will show his authority by stripping the captaincy from Bruno Fernandes and/or dropping Manchester United’s five-times player of the year. On Friday, Carrick refused to deny he may do so, but the bigger picture concerns whether cashing in on the Portuguese and his fellow mutineer, Lisandro Martínez, in the winter window would be prescient to initiate a new era. Fernandes and Martínez are out of contract in the close season (the club has an extra year’s option in both cases) and, judging by recent behaviour, intend to leave. So yielding, say, £40m and £25m respectively for them in January would allow investment as the rebuild begins. Even a few days on, Fernandes’s words in Como seem incredible: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he said after Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation. Fernandes’s open questioning of the tactics is a challenge to the head coach’s authority and we wait to see how/if Carrick will face it down. If Carrick acts and proves he is not a lame duck then even if he is removed a favour is done for his successor. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Mourinho is ready for his clásico return – stock up on popcorn, folks!
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Football Daily has never had much time for conspiracy theories. Lee Harvey Oswald dunnit, Stanley Kubrick didn’t fake the moon landing, Vinícius Jr doesn’t have a body double and Miranda isn’t a secret traitor. But our Spidey senses picked up when the UK government announced their Be Ready campaign on Thursday night. In case you missed it, or live outside the UK and couldn’t care less about this weird little island, we’ve lifted this from our news story : “Every Briton is being urged to stock up to nine litres of bottled water and three days’ worth of food in new government guidance designed to ensure that households can survive a weather, cyber or other serious emergency. The Be Ready campaign is aimed at persuading people to stock up with supplies to last 72 hours, amid growing official concern about the impact of the climate crisis, technological dependency and hostile state threats.” Would it not be much easier all round if the two big clubs in Manchester simply swapped all playing and coaching staff before the next round of fixtures? United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, City would might get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. Sure there’d be a few grumbles from the fans, but more importantly in the current football climate, think of all the potential new shirt sales, and the Us-Against-the-World mentality that Enzo Maresca would be able to instil in his team whose own supporters would even hate them. And no-one would even have to move house. It’s a win-win solution. Although, no, it’s United; so probably a win-high-scoring-draw-against-Wycombe solution” – Justin Kavanagh. Like all right-minded people, I only read Big Website to get my fill of news and information (ahem …). However, I did come across a recent piece in The New Yorker on James Daunt, the chief suit of the US book chain Barnes & Noble (no relation). The billionaire Russian oligarch, Alexander Mamut, asked him 20 years ago how much it would cost to buy Waterstones, and when he was told it would be £40m, he looked pleased and just said, ‘That’s less than Fernando Torres’, before adding, ‘It’s not even half a boat’. Odd reference points these billionaires” – Noble Francis. May I be the first of 1,057 Daniels to say thank you for the good luck message at the end of Thursday’s Football Daily. It has put a little extra pep in my step today” – Daniel Mee. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. item.title: Chaotic state of football in Brazil epitomises a nation where greed has conquered glory | Jonathan Liew
item.description: The national game merely reflects the mood in a divided nation which is going to the polls with very little faith in the power of democracy Look, cards on the table: I don’t know for certain, and nor do you, whether Flávio Bolsonaro – the man widely tipped to become the next president of Brazil after Sunday night’s election – really did steal an island from Richarlison. There are lawyers involved, claims and counter-claims, and in any case, adjudicating land ownership disputes between right-wing strongmen and Tottenham reserve-team strikers lies very much beyond this column’s spectrum of expertise. It’s why, for example, this newspaper took no official position on the well-publicised battle between Rodrigo Duterte and Vincent Janssen over that Polynesian isthmus. According to Richarlison, a few years ago he purchased an island off the southern coast of Rio de Janeiro, and has the documentation to prove it. Richarlison says Bolsonaro tried to buy it from him, and when he refused a lawyer named Willer Tomaz simply turned up and annexed it. “These guys took the island without spending a penny, as far as I know,” Richarlison claimed in an Instagram video that has been viewed more than 31 million times. Tomaz has accused Richarlison of lying, arguing that he has a public deed registered at the notary’s office. Bolsonaro, for his part, has denied any connection with the island in question and described Richarlison’s intervention as “politically motivated”. Continue reading...

item.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou , the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17.
